SL-000007.transcript:
Member (Lucas Cote): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Lucas Cote, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Lucas Cote): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Lucas Cote): Yes, that's right.
Member (Lucas Cote): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Lucas Cote): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Lucas Cote): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Lucas Cote): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with your previous paid claims and the plan booklet.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Lucas Cote): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Lucas Cote): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Lucas Cote): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Lucas Cote): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.
SL-000007.narrative_summary: Lucas Cote, a Sun Life member, contacted support on a declined claim case. Agent Harpreet Gill compared this claim with your previous paid claims and the plan booklet. In the end, it was resolved on this interaction, and the member rated it CSAT 4 (satisfied).

Member (Noah Ahmed): My claim says paid, but the money isn't in my account.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Noah Ahmed, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.

Agent (Priya Sandhu): Did you get a payment notification in the app?
Member (Noah Ahmed): Yes, it says paid on the 4th, but nothing arrived.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Did you update it through the app or with your employer?

Agent (Priya Sandhu): Sun Life keeps its own direct deposit details, separate from your employer's payroll, so a change at work doesn't carry over.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I'm checking where the payment was sent and whether it came back.
Member (Noah Ahmed): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): The payment went to your old bank account and was returned. I've updated your direct deposit and reissued it, so it'll arrive within three business days.
Member (Noah Ahmed): So I'll get it this time?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Yes. I've updated the account and reissued the payment, so it should land within three business days.
Member (Noah Ahmed): Is there anything else going to the old account?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): No, all future claims will go to the new one.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): So the new account is on file and the 120-dollar payment is reissued. You'll see it within three business days.
Member (Noah Ahmed): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-000023.transcript:
Member (Olivia Wilson): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Hi Olivia Wilson, Kevin Nguyen here — let me pull that up.
Member (Olivia Wilson): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Olivia Wilson): The member ID is on the welcome letter.
Member (Olivia Wilson): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Is this the first request or a resubmission?
Member (Olivia Wilson): The second. The first was denied in July.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Did the letter mention any documents that were missing?
Member (Olivia Wilson): No, just that it doesn't meet the criteria.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Has the dental office called us about this directly?
Member (Olivia Wilson): They said they called and got the same answer as me.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Are you in any pain right now?
Member (Olivia Wilson): Some. It's manageable, but I can't chew on that side.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the pre-authorization request and the documents received from the dental office.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): The assessment is done against the plan's criteria for crowns, which are set by Health Canada.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I'm looking at the latest assessment on your file now.
Member (Olivia Wilson): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Olivia Wilson): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Olivia Wilson): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Olivia Wilson): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.
SL-000023.narrative_summary: Olivia Wilson, a Sun Life member, contacted support on a CDCP pre-authorization case. Agent Kevin Nguyen reviewed the pre-authorization request and the documents received from the dental office. In the end, it was resolved on this interaction, and the member rated it CSAT 3 (neutral).

SL-000064.transcript:
Member (Liam O'Brien): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Hi Liam O'Brien, Aisha Rahman here — let me pull that up.
Member (Liam O'Brien): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Liam O'Brien): Yes, that's right.
Member (Liam O'Brien): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Liam O'Brien): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Liam O'Brien): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Liam O'Brien): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Liam O'Brien): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with your previous paid claims and the plan booklet.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Liam O'Brien): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Liam O'Brien): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Liam O'Brien): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Liam O'Brien): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Owen Wilson): I asked to transfer my pension from my old employer's plan to my bank and it still hasn't moved.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Hi Owen Wilson, Kevin Nguyen here — let me pull that up.
Member (Owen Wilson): The market's moved since then and I've lost money waiting.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Owen Wilson): Yes, that's right.
Member (Owen Wilson): The receiving institution says they never got anything.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): When did you send in the transfer request?
Member (Owen Wilson): In June. I signed everything they sent me.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Did the bank send you a transfer form to sign as well?

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Until that form arrives, the funds stay invested in your current options, so they've moved with the market.
Member (Owen Wilson): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): The transfer was held because the receiving institution's form wasn't signed. It came in this morning, so I've released it, and the funds will move within five business days.

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Yes. The form arrived this morning, and I've released the transfer.
Member (Owen Wilson): How long until my bank has it?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Usually five business days, and you'll get a confirmation letter from us.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): So the transfer is released and should reach your bank within five business days.
Member (Owen Wilson): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Noah Fortin): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.

Member (Noah Fortin): Yes, that's right.
Member (Noah Fortin): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Noah Fortin): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Did the letter mention any documents that were missing?
Member (Noah Fortin): No, just that it doesn't meet the criteria.

Agent (Priya Sandhu): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Noah Fortin): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Noah Fortin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Owen Patel): I'm waiting on a decision on my disability claim and nobody has called me.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Owen Patel, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Owen Patel): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?

Member (Owen Patel): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): When did you go off work?
Member (Owen Patel): Six weeks ago. I submitted my part in the first week.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?
Member (Owen Patel): They said about three weeks ago, but I haven't seen anything confirming it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Is there a good number and time to reach you?
Member (Owen Patel): My mobile, any time before three. I have appointments in the afternoons.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?

Member (Owen Patel): Is there anything I can do to speed it up?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Ask HR for the date they sent the statement. If it's missing, that's the one thing holding the file.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: the file is waiting on the employer's statement, your case manager has been asked to call you, and I've noted your preferred contact times.

Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

SL-000907.transcript:
Member (Gurpreet Ahmed): My medication claim was put on hold for more information and I don't know what you need.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Hi Gurpreet Ahmed, Marc Tremblay here — let me pull that up.
Member (Gurpreet Ahmed): I uploaded the prescription through the app already.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Gurpreet Ahmed): Yes, that's right.
Member (Gurpreet Ahmed): My doctor charges 45 dollars to fill in forms.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Which medication or service is the request about?
Member (Gurpreet Ahmed): A new medication my specialist started me on last week.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Did the pharmacy give you the name of the form they need?
Member (Gurpreet Ahmed): They said 'prior authorization' and gave me a number to call. That's it.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Which pharmacy are you using?
Member (Gurpreet Ahmed): The one near my work. They said they can resubmit as soon as it's approved.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): How much medication do you have left?
Member (Gurpreet Ahmed): About four days. That's why I'm calling now.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Let me take a look. I've checked the information request and the documents already on file.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): For this medication the plan needs a prior authorization from your doctor, not just the prescription.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I'm checking whether anything from your doctor's office is already on file.
Member (Gurpreet Ahmed): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The prior authorization form is on file from last week. It just wasn't linked to the drug claim. I've linked it, and the pharmacy can resubmit today.
Member (Gurpreet Ahmed): So I can pick it up today?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Yes. The authorization is linked to the claim now, so the pharmacy can resubmit and it should go through.
Member (Gurpreet Ahmed): Will I have to do this every time?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): No. It's approved for twelve months, so refills go through automatically.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): So you're all set: the authorization is on file for twelve months and the pharmacy can process it today.
Member (Gurpreet Ahmed): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Hannah Campbell): 750 dollars on the 1st.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Is the payment still coming from the same bank account?

Member (Hannah Campbell): Maybe, if it's affordable.

Member (Hannah Campbell): How much would a lower amount cost?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Halving the coverage brings it to about 375 dollars a month. The comparison I'm sending shows a few options.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: the new rate follows the renewal schedule, I've sent you the notice and a lower-coverage option, and you can decide within 30 days.

Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Chantal Kim): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Chantal Kim): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Chantal Kim): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Chantal Kim): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?

Agent (Sophie Belanger): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Chantal Kim): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Chantal Kim): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Chantal Kim): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Chantal Kim): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Arjun Martin): My Canadian Dental Care Plan crown request was denied and even the supervisor couldn't tell me why.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Arjun Martin, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Arjun Martin): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Arjun Martin): Yes, that's right.
Member (Arjun Martin): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Arjun Martin): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Is this the first request or a resubmission?
Member (Arjun Martin): The second. The first was denied in July.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Did the letter mention any documents that were missing?
Member (Arjun Martin): No, just that it doesn't meet the criteria.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Are you in any pain right now?
Member (Arjun Martin): Some. It's manageable, but I can't chew on that side.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the pre-authorization request and the documents received from the dental office.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The assessment is done against the plan's criteria for crowns, which are set by Health Canada.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I'm looking at the latest assessment on your file now.
Member (Arjun Martin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Arjun Martin): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Arjun Martin): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Arjun Martin): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Arjun Martin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Fatima Roy): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Fatima Roy): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Fatima Roy): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Fatima Roy): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Emma Martin, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.

Member (Emma Martin): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Emma Martin): Can I appeal it?

Member (Chantal O'Brien): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?

Agent (Marc Tremblay): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Chantal O'Brien): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Chantal O'Brien): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Chantal O'Brien): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.

Member (Emma Roy): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Emma Roy): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Emma Roy): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Emma Roy): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.

Member (Liam Cote): I'm following up again — I was told on the phone that physio was covered, and now two of my claims have been declined.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Liam Cote, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Liam Cote): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Liam Cote): The explanation of benefits just shows a code. It doesn't say why.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.

Member (Liam Cote): Yes, that's right.
Member (Liam Cote): I have the date I called and the name of the person who told me it was fully covered.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Do you remember roughly when you called to check the coverage?
Member (Liam Cote): It was the week before my first appointment, early last month. I wrote the date down because I wanted to be sure.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): What were you told on that call, as best you remember?
Member (Liam Cote): That physiotherapy was covered at 80% and I didn't need anything else. Nobody mentioned a referral.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): How many sessions have you had so far?
Member (Liam Cote): Four. I paid for all of them up front and submitted them together.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Has your clinic been in touch with us at all?

Agent (Priya Sandhu): You can get the referral from your doctor now. Anything from that date forward will be covered, and I'll note that on your file as well.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: a review request is open with your call note attached, you should hear back within five business days, and a referral from your doctor covers any visits after today.
Member (Liam Cote): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.
